research_question: Owned-page scope: AI in Law Firms Statistics. Planned sources and method: ABA AI-use survey and firm policy sample; distinguish individual and approved use. Build a source-labelled comparison covering lawyer AI adoption and law firm AI policy; record dates, definitions and sample limits. Sources are proposed, not verified findings.

research_brief.purpose: Give law firm leaders the clearest 2026 figures on AI use in law firms, separated into personal use, organizational use, training and governance, unauthorized use, and client pricing pressure, with the population and limits of each source.
research_brief.audience: Managing partners, innovation and knowledge leads, general counsel, legal operations professionals, and researchers who cite AI adoption figures.
research_brief.data_period: 8am 2026 Legal Industry Report as summarized April 1, 2026 (with its 2025 comparison); Thomson Reuters publisher summary dated July 2, 2026 (2025 and 2026); Thomson Reuters Future of Professionals 2026 legal report (fieldwork March and April 2026)
research_brief.scope_limitations: Desk research from public summaries. The 8am figures come from sponsored content written by LawPay on the ABA site; the full report was not read and its sample is not stated on the page. Thomson Reuters figures are organization-level in the blog and respondent-level in the legal report, which covers 46 countries (421 of 736 law firm responses from the United States). No figure is presented as a U.S.-only census.

competitors.covered_well: Brings several 2026 vendor surveys together with firm-size detail.
competitors.gaps: Does not separate personal from firm use, omits unauthorized use, and has no charts or reporting framework.

content_gaps: Reviewed pages rarely state who was counted, and none sets personal use, firm use, and corporate legal use side by side with their limits.
Unauthorized AI use and missing AI strategy are absent from four of five reviewed pages.
Client pricing expectations are not shown against what firms have changed.
No reviewed page labels sponsored survey summaries as such or gives a firm-level reporting model.
value_add: Each 2026 figure is tied to its respondent group and source type, including a clear sponsored-content label, with four charts and four tables, the client-expectation gap from the Thomson Reuters legal report with its 736-response sample, a five-state policy inventory, a pilot test checklist, and a five-panel reporting model.

claims.statement: 69% of legal professionals personally use generative AI for work (31% in the 2025 report); uses, time saved, barriers (46%, 42%, 39%, 39%), and 54% with no training and no plans.
41% of law firms and 47% of corporate legal departments were using generative AI in 2026, up from 28% and 23%; 53% of adopters report seeing a return.

34% unauthorized use; 20% no AI strategy in practice; 71% of in-house professionals expect commercial model change and 28% of firms changed pricing; 77% and 5% on AI-enabled quality; 24% and 36% on declining jobs; 736 law firm responses in 46 countries with 421 from the United States, gathered March and April 2026.
